title: Systems of Equations
summary: A system asks for values satisfying several equations at once. Solve linear systems by substitution or elimination; nonlinear systems (a line and a circle) by substitution. A system has one solution, none (parallel), or infinitely many (same line).

system of equations.plain: Two or more equations solved together.
system of equations.in_class: A solution satisfies all of them.

substitution.plain: Solve one equation for a variable, plug into the other.

elimination.plain: Add/subtract equations to cancel a variable.

inconsistent.in_class: Parallel lines; elimination gives a false statement.

point of intersection.plain: Where the graphs meet — the solution.

concept_sections.heading: Substitution
concept_sections.explanation: Solve one equation for a variable, substitute into the other, solve the single-variable equation, then back-substitute for the second variable.
math_steps: Isolate a variable in one equation.

concept_sections.heading: Elimination
concept_sections.explanation: Scale the equations so one variable's coefficients are opposites, add to cancel it, solve for the remaining variable, then back-substitute.

concept_sections.heading: Number of solutions
concept_sections.explanation: One intersection ⇒ one solution; parallel lines ⇒ none (inconsistent); identical lines ⇒ infinitely many (dependent). Elimination reveals which via $0=0$ or $0=c$.

concept_sections.heading: Nonlinear systems
concept_sections.explanation: For a line and a conic, substitute the line into the conic to get a quadratic; its solutions give the intersection points (0, 1, or 2).
math_steps: Solve the linear equation for one variable.

concept_sections.heading: Word problems with systems
concept_sections.explanation: Mixture, rate, and money problems often need two equations. Define two variables, write two relationships, and solve the system.
math_steps: Write two equations from the conditions.
